week_thesis: Three sector themes converge amid a challenging macro backdrop (CPI 3.8%, Iran war driving Brent crude to $102-110/bbl, S&P 500 at 7,408 after -1.24% Friday selloff on Iran/inflation fears). Q1 2026 earnings season has been exceptional. Strategy avoids all high-multiple tech exposed to this week's NVDA earnings (Wednesday) and manages rate sensitivity. Picks: (1) AMAT — semiconductor equipment cycle acceleration confirmed by Q2 beat (May 14: EPS $2.86 vs $2.68 est, revenue $7.91B +11.4% YoY, Q3 guided to $8.95B above consensus), Deutsche Bank raised PT to $550 from $450 (Buy); (2) LLY — GLP-1 market dominance (60.1% U.S. share), Q1 revenue $19.8B +56% YoY, EPS $8.55 beat by 28%, PT $1,218 (21% upside), defensive healthcare in risk-off environment; (3) EOG — direct Iran war energy beneficiary, Q1 EPS $3.41 beat on May 5, revenue +22%, $1.5B FCF, Goldman Sachs sees Brent >$100/bbl through 2026. Deliberate avoids: NVDA (earnings Wed), WMT/HD (earnings this week), UNH (earnings Tue), PLTR (150x P/E too risky in rising-rate/risk-off setup, we were already burned last week).

buys.reasoning: Applied Materials Q2 FY2026 (reported May 14): EPS $2.86 vs $2.68 est (+6.7% beat), revenue $7.91B +11.4% YoY, beat consensus by 2.8%. Non-GAAP gross margin 50%, operating margin 32.1% — both expanding. Q3 guidance: ~$8.95B revenue and EPS ~$3.36, both above consensus. Management cited semiconductor equipment business growing >30% in calendar 2026, advanced packaging >50%. Deutsche Bank raised PT to $550 from $450 (Buy). Stock 'surged' post-earnings (Seeking Alpha: 'Applied Materials pops as Q2 results, guidance top estimates'). Technical: RS60 +26.1%, dip5d -2.4%, RSI 57 — healthy pullback entry post-earnings pop. No earnings this week. NVDA earnings Wed are a potential sector catalyst if beat (consensus: $79.2B revenue, 72% FY2027 growth). High conviction on semi equipment cycle acceleration.

Eli Lilly Q1 2026 (reported April 30): Revenue $19.8B +56% YoY, adj EPS $8.55 beat by 28%. Mounjaro + Zepbound = 60.1% U.S. GLP-1 market share. Zepbound Q1 U.S. revenue $4.16B (+80% YoY). FY2026 guidance raised to $82-85B. Oral weight loss pill Foundayo launched. Pipeline: retatrutide triple agonist months from launch. 30/30 analyst coverage: 23 Buy, 2 Strong Buy, 4 Hold, 1 Sell. Consensus PT $1,218 (21% upside from current ~$900-1,000 range). Morgan Stanley/Wolfe Research high-end targets $1,325-1,344. FDA liver-failure report on GLP-1 drug is a known risk but manageable. Technical: RS60 +19.1%, dip5d -3.8%, RSI 50.6 — mid-range RSI with room to run, 3.8% pullback as entry point. Defensive healthcare in risk-off/inflation environment provides relative stability versus high-multiple growth names. Already reported April 30 — no earnings risk this week.

EOG Resources Q1 2026 (reported May 5): EPS $3.41 beat estimates by $0.18, revenue $6.92B +22.1% YoY. $1.5B free cash flow supports $25B+ shareholder return plan. Production guidance raised. Iran war directly drives thesis: Strait of Hormuz disruption is 'largest supply disruption in history of global oil market' per IEA. WTI at $102/bbl, Brent ~$107. EIA projects Brent avg $106/bbl in May-June. Goldman Sachs sees Brent >$100/bbl through 2026 if Strait restrictions persist. EOG +11% since Iran war began per search. US shale E&P (Devon, EOG, OXY) are primary beneficiaries. Trump comments on Iran ceasefire 'on massive life support' signals prolonged conflict = sustained high oil prices. Technical: RS60 +26.4%, dip5d -0.7%, RSI 54.7 — steady momentum, minimal dip. Already reported Q1 — no earnings risk this week.

Current price ~$132 (down from $147 bars), 52-week low $118.93. We were already burned -3.52% on PLTR last week. Memory lesson: 'Strong fundamental thesis does not guarantee near-term price action.' AVOID until macro stabilizes or multiple compresses.
